title: upgrade: attention kernels -> FlashAttnV2 + fused ops, rope/rotary optimizations, KV batching & scheduler tuning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: We saw regressions for long-context workloads on newer open models and inconsistent latency for short/long tails in mixed workloads. This PR upgrades our attention kernels to the FlashAttentionV2 baseline, introduces fused rotary/rope ops where applicable, and adds a compatible fused-ops path for KV cache hot paths. It also includes scheduler-level heuristics to prefer KV-friendly batching and soft-priority routing for short-latency requests.

What this PR does (summary):
- Integrates FlashAttentionV2 kernels (C++/CUDA) with our kernel-selection layer and adds runtime toggles for per-model force_enable/auto.
- Adds fused rotary/rope operators (CPU fallback + CUDA fused ops) to eliminate separate elementwise ops and reduce memory passes.
- Implements a fused KV gather/concat path used on cache hits to reduce device-host synchronization and memory copies.
- Enhances the continuous-batching scheduler: new priority buckets for short requests, KV-aware batch assembly, and a micro-batching fallback for very high-concurrency scenarios.
- Adds end-to-end tests and microbench harness for perf regression tracking, plus new metrics (attn_kernel, fused_ops_used, kv_copy_bytes, scheduler_bucket_latency).

Motivation: The combined changes reduce p99 latency for ~2k context workloads and improve tokens/sec for long sequences by decreasing memory bandwidth and kernel launch overhead. This unlocks better throughput for Dedicated customers with mixed tail latency requirements.

Notes: The fused ops keep the existing API surface; model semantics preserved. We added runtime feature gates and model config annotations to opt-in per-model while we ramp.

Related: ENG-12456 (kernel upgrades roadmap), ENG-13002 (kv-batching heuristics), SUP-501 (customer report: long-context slowdown).
